title: Budget responses reveal housing affordability pressures
summary:
Responses to the government's recent budget have highlighted persistent challenges facing potential homebuyers and property owners across income brackets. Young professionals remain priced out of the market while high earners struggle with mortgage costs and frozen tax thresholds.

title: Landlord database upload could take agents 714 days
summary:
Large letting agencies managing 10,000 rental properties could require 714 working days to upload data onto the new national landlord register, according to calculations presented to MPs. The figure is based on 30 minutes per property and 70 data points required for each entry, with no provision for bulk uploading.

title: Rental property registration guidance issued for agents
summary:
The government has released guidance for letting agents and property managers on the mandatory rental property registration system coming into force across England from December 2026. Registration begins in the West Midlands on 15 December 2026, with a phased rollout across all English regions concluding in November 2027.

The post Rental property registration guidance issued for agents appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: OBR revises house price forecasts downward for 2026
summary:
The Office for Budget Responsibility has lowered its house price growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027, citing elevated mortgage rates and stagnating wage growth as constraining factors. Property transactions are also expected to decline 4% compared to previous estimates.

The post OBR revises house price forecasts downward for 2026 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Income tax on rental earnings to rise by 2% from April 2027
summary:
Chancellor John Healey has announced a further 2% increase in income tax on rental earnings from April 2027, bringing the basic rate to 24%. Industry bodies warn the measure will drive up rents and reduce rental supply as landlords face mounting cost pressures.

title: Embassy conversions spark planning disputes in London
summary:
A Pimlico resident has launched a judicial review against Westminster City Council over a neighbouring property's conversion to the Montenegro embassy. The case highlights growing tensions between diplomatic property changes and residential concerns in central London's prime areas.

The post Embassy conversions spark planning disputes in London appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Government confirms £2m mansion tax from March 2028
summary:
The Government has confirmed plans to introduce a High Value Council Tax Surcharge on properties valued at £2 million or more, with bills set to commence from March 2028. Chancellor John Healey's Autumn Budget outlined details of the tax structure, including exemptions and deferral schemes.

The post Government confirms £2m mansion tax from March 2028 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Digital mortgage deed signing launched by LMS
summary:
Conveyancing services provider LMS has launched Qualified Electronic Signatures for mortgage deed signing, allowing participating lenders and law firms to offer digital signing to customers. The service is currently being used by lenders through LMS's fee-assisted remortgage service.

The post Digital mortgage deed signing launched by LMS appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Ombudsman orders refund over unmortgageable property sale
summary:
A property business has been ordered to refund a £4,000 buyer's premium and pay additional compensation after failing to verify material information about an investment property's mortgageability. The Property Ombudsman ruled the agent could not rely on contractual refund deadlines when the problem arose from its own failure to verify material information.

The post Ombudsman orders refund over unmortgageable property sale appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Downing provides £18.4m for Hertfordshire heritage scheme
summary:
Downing has provided £18.4 million in development finance to a regional developer for the conversion of the former Princess Helena College at Temple Dinsley in Preston, Hertfordshire, into 40 apartments and three houses. The financing will support the restoration of the Grade II* listed main building alongside the construction of 24 new-build homes.
